references.text: Elijah stretches himself over the dead boy and cries out to the Lord, and the boy comes back to life. A parallel to Jesus raising the widow's son from the dead in Nain.
Elisha raises the Shunammite woman's son from the dead. Both Elijah, Elisha, and Jesus raise a mother's only son back to life.
A dead man thrown into Elisha's tomb comes back to life when he touches Elisha's bones. Physical contact in connection with resurrection from the dead, just as Jesus touches the bier.
Jesus raises Jairus' daughter from the dead with the words "Child, get up!" — a similar command to "Young man, I say to you: Get up!" in Luke 7:14.
Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead by crying out with a loud voice: "Lazarus, come out!" A parallel where Jesus, with an authoritative word, commands the dead to get up.
Peter raises Tabitha from the dead with the words "Tabitha, get up!" — a clear parallel to Jesus' words at the resurrection in Nain.
The immediate effect of Jesus' words: the dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother — a parallel to Elijah's raising (1 Kings 17:23).
Jesus raises Jairus' daughter from the dead and says "Talitha kumi" (Little girl, get up). Same pattern: Jesus speaks directly to the dead with a command to get up.
